outlier: Q4 2021 user survey results: about null safety, ecosystem, text editing, and mobile development

recent_posts.title: Introducing Skills for Dart and Flutter
recent_posts.summary: The Flutter team is introducing Agent Skills for Dart and Flutter — domain-specific instruction sets that teach AI coding agents how to complete common Flutter and Dart development tasks. Unlike MCP which provides tools, Skills provide task-oriented workflows and instructions, improving accuracy and reducing token usage. Five initial skills are available covering integration testing, localization setup, responsive layouts, Dart pattern matching, and test coverage collection. Skills are installed via npx and work with any AI agent.

recent_posts.title: Saying goodbye to CocoaPods: Swift Package Manager is soon the default in Flutter!
recent_posts.summary: Flutter 3.44 will make Swift Package Manager (SwiftPM) the default dependency manager for iOS and macOS apps, replacing CocoaPods. This change is driven by CocoaPods entering maintenance mode and its registry becoming read-only on December 2, 2026. The Flutter CLI will automatically handle migration for app developers. Plugin developers must add SwiftPM support by adding a Package.swift file; 61% of the top 100 iOS plugins have already migrated. Plugins without SwiftPM support will receive lower pub.dev scores. A temporary opt-out is available via pubspec.yaml if issues arise.

recent_posts.title: That’s a wrap: Everything Flutter at Google Cloud Next
recent_posts.summary: Flutter and Dart team highlights from Google Cloud Next include a preview of Dart support for Firebase Functions enabling full-stack Dart development, the Dart Admin SDK for Firebase, and a GenUI-powered AI coffee shop demo. Enterprise customers Toyota and Talabat shared how Flutter powers their products. Sessions covered Generative UI and full-stack Dart, with more content promised at Google I/O 2026.

recent_posts.title: We rebuilt Flutter’s websites with Dart and Jaspr
recent_posts.summary: Flutter's team migrated dart.dev, flutter.dev, and docs.flutter.dev from a fragmented stack (Eleventy/Node.js and Wagtail/Python) to a unified Dart-based setup using Jaspr, an open-source web framework. Jaspr supports client-side rendering, server-side rendering, and static site generation, with a component model familiar to Flutter developers. Key benefits include a single Dart toolchain, partial hydration for performance and SEO, Markdown-driven content via Jaspr Content, and seamless use of new Dart features like dot shorthands, null-aware collection elements, and WebAssembly compilation. The migration was a collaborative effort with Jaspr's creator Kilian, who also built out Jaspr Content to meet the sites' needs.

recent_posts.title: Flutter’s Material and Cupertino code freeze
recent_posts.summary: Flutter's Material and Cupertino libraries are now frozen in the flutter/flutter repository as of April 7th. This is the first step toward decoupling them into standalone pub.dev packages: material_ui and cupertino_ui. The freeze applies only to contributors; app developers are unaffected for now. After the Flutter 3.44 stable release, the new packages will be published, and developers will eventually need to migrate. The old code will be deprecated in the release after 3.44 and later deleted. Open PRs will be ported to flutter/packages, and detailed migration instructions will follow when the time comes.

recent_posts.title: How Dart and Flutter are thinking about AI in 2026
recent_posts.summary: The Flutter and Dart team shares their strategic thinking on AI integration for 2026, addressing three developer personas: traditional developers, AI-assisted developers, and AI-first developers. Key data points include 79% of Flutter developers using AI assistants and a 46% trust gap in AI accuracy. The team outlines guiding principles including 'humans first' language design, agent-agnostic open standards via MCP, and reducing the 'verification tax' through quality AI-generated code. Collaborations with Google DeepMind and Antigravity are mentioned, along with MCP tooling for hot reload during AI-assisted development.

recent_posts.title: Jaime’s build context: Prompt engineering as infrastructure
recent_posts.summary: AI agents can generate code rapidly, but the real challenge is maintaining code integrity at scale. The solution is treating prompts as version-controlled infrastructure through Agent Skills—an open standard that packages AI instructions into reusable, reproducible workflows. By anchoring agent workflows in CI/CD feedback loops, deterministic testing, and structured prompts, teams can bridge the gap between traditional manual coding and high-velocity AI-assisted development. Skills transform tribal knowledge into executable documentation, ensuring consistent, high-quality results across the entire team while maintaining code health through automated verification gates.

recent_posts.title: What’s new in Flutter 3.38
recent_posts.summary: Flutter 3.38 introduces dot shorthands for more concise Dart code, allowing developers to omit inferable types. The release includes enhanced Widget Previews with IDE integration, web development configuration files with proxy settings, and expanded hot reload support. Material and Cupertino libraries receive API consistency improvements with the WidgetState migration. iOS developers benefit from UIScene lifecycle support (required for future iOS releases) and devicectl deployment eliminating Xcode app launches. Android updates include 16KB page size compatibility with NDK r28, memory leak fixes, and updated dependency versions. The framework adds OverlayPortal enhancements, predictive back navigation, Windows display management, and improved accessibility features including SliverSemantics. DevTools improvements address network panel usability and Flutter Inspector bugs.

recent_posts.title: Announcing Flutter 3.38 & Dart 3.10: Building the future of apps
recent_posts.summary: Flutter 3.38 and Dart 3.10 are now available with significant improvements to developer productivity and AI integration. Key features include Dart's dot shorthands for more concise code, stable build hooks for native asset bundling, and Flutter's web enhancements with hot reload support. The release introduces Flutter GenUI SDK for building dynamic AI-powered UIs, Firebase AI integration samples, and Gemini CLI extension. Platform updates include full iOS 26/Xcode 26 support, Android NDK r28 for 16KB page size compatibility, predictive back gestures on Android, and enhanced accessibility features. Developer tooling improvements include an experimental Widget Previewer and new analyzer plugin system.

recent_posts.title: What’s new in Flutter 3.32
recent_posts.summary: Flutter 3.32 introduces exciting new features like experimental hot reload for web applications, enhanced Cupertino squircles for native iOS app design, and deeper AI integrations with Firebase. This release, shaped by over 1000 commits from the community, offers expanded functionality and improvements across web, iOS, and Android platforms including advancements in accessibility and DevTools. The update also covers performance optimizations and breaking changes such as deprecations for older systems and packages.

top_posts.title: Announcing Flutter for Windows
top_posts.summary: Announcing Flutter for Windows Build high-quality Windows apps that also run on mobile and web. In 2021, Flutter became the most popular cross-platform UI toolkit. Nearly half a million apps use Flutter… So far, we’ve seen momentum that has exceeded our expectations.

top_posts.title: What’s new in Flutter 3.7
top_posts.summary: The team is pleased to announce that the new Impeller rendering engine is ready for preview on iOS on the stable channel. For all platforms, you can define a Material Design menu that provides cascading menu bars. The DevTools Memory debugging tool has undergone a complete overhaul. There are three new feature tabs, Profile, Trace and Diff.

top_posts.title: Announcing Flutter 2.8
top_posts.summary: Flutter aims to change how apps are built. It unites mobile, web, desktop, and embedded development into a single toolkit. The latest update makes it easier than ever to connect apps to back-end services, such as Firebase and Google Cloud. It adds production-quality support for Google Ads and major upgrades to the camera and embedded web plugins.

top_posts.title: What’s new in Flutter 3.27
top_posts.summary: Flutter 3.27 introduces significant updates and features, including enhancements to Cupertino widgets, the introduction of Impeller as the default rendering engine for modern Android devices, and new options in DevTools to streamline app management. This release also brings improvements in performance, fidelity, and theming across the Flutter framework for better development consistency.

top_posts.title: Supernova: a design system platform
top_posts.summary: Supernova is a design system platform built with Flutter and exports code for Flutter. CEO Jiří Třečák and CTO Artem Ufimtcev talk about what they have built. Supernova was written as a native macOS app, but saw lots of interest in a web-based solution.
